Stroma showed infiltration by chronic inflammatory cells and melanophages (Fig. 1 and Fig. 2). Foreign body giant cell reaction was seen. The resected surgical margins were free from the tumour. Immunohistochemistry of tissue sections were negative for HMB45 (Fig. 3) and S100 (Fig. 4) and positive for pankeratin. A final histopathological diagnosis of Pigmented Basal cell carcinoma of nipple and areola was made. Patient was followed up for one year, no recurrence or metastasis noted.

in_text_mentions: arranged as interconnecting cords in between myxoid matrix. Focal areas showed melanin pigment in tumour cells. Stroma showed infiltration by chronic inflammatory cells and melanophages (Fig. 1 and Fig. 2). Foreign body giant cell reaction was seen. The resected surgical margins were free from the tumour. Immunohistochemistry of tissue sections were negative for HMB45 (Fig. 3) and S100 (Fig. 4) and positive for pankeratin. A final histopathological diagnosis of Pigmented Basal cell carcinoma of nipple and areola was made. Patient was followed up for one year, no recurrence or metastasis noted.

in_text_mentions: routine sun exposure. There were no systemic symptoms. Cutaneous examination revealed a solitary well-defined hyperpigmented plaque measuring 3 × 4 cm with raised pigmented margins near the left ear (Fig. 1). There was no ulceration or regional lymphadenopathy. Systemic examination was normal. A clinical diagnosis of pigmented basal cell carcinoma was made. Biopsy from the edge of the plaque showed multiple nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading in the papillary dermis in continuity with the overlying epithelium (Figs. 2 and 3). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E of pigmented basal cell carcinoma showing subjacent basaloid nests; article final diagnosis confirms pigmented basal cell carcinoma with melanin pigment within nests. B: Higher magnification H&E shows tumor arising from basal layer with peripheral nuclear palisading and melanin pigment/melanocytes within nests, classic for pigmented BCC. C: p63 IHC shows basaloid tumor nests of same pigmented basal cell carcinoma confirmed by H&E pigment and final diagnosis. D: CK5/6 IHC shows basaloid tumor nests of same pigmented basal cell carcinoma confirmed by H&E pigment and final diagnosis.
panels.attribution_text: Fuentes-Calvo et al. Pigmented basal cell carcinoma of the anus: a rare entity with diagnostic challenges.. Journal of surgical case reports 2024. doi:10.1093/jscr/rjae554. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. (A) Display of normal stratified flat epithelium of the skin with a subjacent neoplasm featuring small nests. (B) Higher magnification reveals the tumor arising from the basal layer of the skin (*). The nests exhibit characteristic peripheral nuclear palisading (black arrows), and both melanin pigment and melanocytes are visible (white arrows). (C) Both the tumor and adjacent skin cells exhibit strong nuclear positivity for p63. (D) Tumor cells demonstrate strong positivity for high molecular weight cytokeratins (CK5/6).
in_text_mentions: roscopically, the hematoxylin and eosin-stained sections revealed a malignant tumor characterized by nests of cells with scant to moderate cytoplasm and basophilic nuclei, exhibiting peripheral nuclear palisading. Melanocytes and melanin pigment were observed within the tumor nests and stroma. Immunohistochemical tests showed positive results for p63 and CK5/6 (Fig. 1), and negative results for HMB-45. Additionally, intense and diffuse positivity for BCL2 was noted (Fig. 2). The final diagnosis confirmed a pigmented basal cell carcinoma with infiltrative, micronodular, and ulcerative patterns.
